references.text: The day before, John had pointed out Jesus as the "Lamb of God" ([ref:Joh 1:29|John 1:29]). Now, "the next day" (Τῇ ἐπαύριον), John stands there again and repeats his testimony (v. 36), showing the connection between the two days.

The immediate continuation of this verse: John sees Jesus walking by and says, "Look, the Lamb of God!" and the two disciples follow Jesus ([ref:Joh 1:36-37|John 1:36-37]). Verse 35 sets the scene for the disciples leaving John to follow Jesus.
One of the two disciples who were with John in verse 35 is identified as Andrew, Simon Peter's brother ([ref:Joh 1:40|John 1:40]). This reveals who "the two" (δύο) in verse 35 were.

The disciples of John the Baptist come to him and tell him that everyone is going to Jesus. John answers that he is not the Christ, but was sent ahead, and that "he must increase, I must decrease" ([ref:Joh 3:26-30|John 3:26-30]). This reflects the transition that begins in 1:35, where John's disciples leave him to follow Jesus.

Jesus returns to the place where John first baptized, and many come to believe because "everything John said about him was true" ([ref:Joh 10:40-42|John 10:40-42]). John's testimony, which began with scenes like those in 1:35, bears fruit even later.

John's role as a witness is introduced in the prologue: "There came a man sent from God; his name was John. He came to testify" ([ref:Joh 1:6-8|John 1:6-8]). In 1:35 we see this mission in practice, with John standing ready with his disciples to point them toward Jesus.

Peter describes that the new apostle must be someone who followed Jesus "from John's baptism" ([ref:Apg 1:21-22|Acts 1:21-22]). This confirms that several of Jesus' first disciples originally came from the circle around John the Baptist, as we see in John 1:35.

Paul meets disciples in Ephesus who only knew John's baptism ([ref:Apg 19:1-4|Acts 19:1-4]). This shows that John the Baptist had disciples (μαθηταί) spread over large areas, and that his ministry pointed onward to Jesus – as happens concretely in John 1:35.
